thread:
elya: Heads-up — running canary soak at ~2k qps (model: redwood-v2-small, seq=1024). Seeing p99 tail spikes when KV cache starts evicting under sustained pressure. p95 is stable but p99 jumps from ~120ms to ~1.7s within ~30s window.

samir: can you paste the numbers and config? microbatch size / batch timeout / kv size? :eyes:

elya: microbatch_size=32, batch_timeout_ms=8, kv_cache_max=6GB, eviction_policy=LRU-ish adaptive. Observed evictions/sec ~45-60 when qps hits 1800+. Quick perf snapshot: ```p50: 22ms
p95: 115ms
p99: 870ms
p999: 1.72s
evictions/sec: 52
active_workers: 48
avg_batch_tokens: 68```

nora: hm that p99 curve looks like KV lookup stalls not compute. Do you see IO spikes or kernel stalls (ctx switch)?

elya: attached a short perf profile — looks like long wait on kv-shard::evict_lock plus a handful of threads hitting slow path in kernel-selector after eviction. When eviction runs we see increased kernel selection jitter and batching throughput drops.

jess: is this after the recent kernel selection patch? that changed fallback order for quantized kernels. Could be changing per-token latency distribution under partial cache misses.

elya: yes rolled kernel-selector v1.14 in the canary 1.5h before soak start. Reverted locally and p99 improved back down to ~190ms in quick test. Not identical env though.

samir: interesting. Two hypotheses: 1) eviction pauses are contending with microbatch assembly (locks) causing some requests to get pushed to single-thread kernel path -> huge tail. 2) kernel-selector change increases cost on cold KV hits because it probes more kernels before choosing fallback -> multiplies stall.

nora: agree. Also microbatch sizing matters: with size=32 a single thread missing KV can force other requests to wait on KV retrieval + lock. Try reducing microbatch to 16 or enable non-blocking KV lookup path (prefetch).

elya: ran short AB: microbatch=16 -> p99 drops to ~420ms (still worse than baseline). microbatch=8 -> p99 ~210ms, throughput drops ~12%. So it's a clear latency vs throughput tradeoff.

jess: we shouldn't immediately revert kernel patch if it improves steady throughput. Let's instrument kernel selector to count "kernel probes per request" and track average added latency on a cold KV miss. Also add metrics for per-request kv-wait time and whether request used fallback kernel vs fast path.

infra-bot: deploy v1.14 -> canary group a finished at 2027-06-09T14:12:04Z :white_check_mark:

samir: good. Actionable plan: (1) add metrics (kv_wait_ms, kernel_probes, used_fallback) — short PR, (2) add opt-in non-blocking KV prefetch for microbatch pipeline, (3) run controlled sweep: microbatch sizes [8,16,32], kv_cache sizes [6GB,8GB,10GB], kernel-selector v1.13 vs v1.14 to quantify p95/p99/throughput.

nora: also add an eviction stress benchmark that reproduces high concurrency pattern (random key churn + seq=1024) so we can simulate before rolling patches.

elya: noted. I'll open the benchmark + metrics PRs and kick off the param sweep tomorrow. For immediate mitigation on canary I'll set microbatch=16 and bump kv_cache to 8GB to reduce eviction frequency.

jess: :thumbsup: keep us posted. If we see any regressions, revert kernel-selector on prod.

samir: one more note — if kernel probes are cheap but multiply due to repeated probes per-token, consider caching the chosen kernel per-model+seq_len for short TTL. That could reduce selector cost on cold misses.

elya: good idea. adding as dash item. I'll paste the preliminary benchmark results once sweep completes.

nora: thanks all — this matches a few customer reports about intermittent p99s under high concurrency. Great triage so far. :heart:
